fields.claim_quote: we conclude that no maximum-weight edge of any cycle in G can belong to the MST.
fields.complete_source:
Solution:
Proof. Let G = (V, E) be a connected graph with edge weights w : E →R. Let
T be a minimum spanning tree (MST) of G. We will prove that for any cycle
C in G, the maximum-weight edge in C does not belong to T.
Consider any cycle C in G, and let emax be the edge of maximum weight in
C. Suppose for contradiction that emax ∈T.
Since T is a spanning tree, removing emax from T disconnects T into two
subtrees T1 and T2. The cycle C must contain at least one other edge e′ ̸= emax
that connects T1 and T2, because C is a cycle containing emax and must return
to its starting vertex.
Now consider the spanning tree T ′ formed by removing emax from T and
adding e′:
T ′ = (T \ {emax}) ∪{e′}
We have:
[U+0088 CONTROL] T ′ is connected because e′ reconnects T1 and T2.
[U+0088 CONTROL] T ′ has no cycles because it has exactly |V | −1 edges (same as T) and is
connected.
Moreover, since emax is the maximum-weight edge in C, we have w(e′) <
w(emax). Therefore:
w(T ′) = w(T) −w(emax) + w(e′) < w(T)
This contradicts the minimality of T.
Hence our initial assumption that
emax ∈T must be false, and we conclude that no maximum-weight edge of any
cycle in G can belong to the MST.
2
fields.explanation: The original1,2,2 triangle is retained; the certified tree{01,12} is the original T2. It contains a tied maximum. Every MST contains some maximum; no claim is made that one fixed tied maximum belongs to every MST. The selected theorem certifies the source-qualified primary counterexample. Historical auxiliary sweeps are not silently promoted to universal statements. The original nearby repair is to require a unique strict maximum on the cycle. If an MST contained that edge, deleting it would split the tree into two components. Another cycle edge crosses this cut and has strictly smaller weight, so exchanging the edges would produce a lighter spanning tree. Ties destroy precisely this strict inequality.
fields.flaw: Keep the triangle V={0,1,2} with weights w01=1 and w02=w12=2. Its two minimum spanning trees are T1={01,02} and T2={01,12}, both of weight 3; the third spanning tree has weight 4. Edge 12 is a maximum-weight edge of the cycle and belongs to T2, contradicting the claim that a maximum-weight cycle edge belongs to no MST. Each MST contains some maximum edge, although no fixed tied maximum edge belongs to every MST.

Problem Statement
Problem: Algorithms - 18
Suppose G = (V, E) is a connected graph with weighted edges. Establish that for any
cycle in G, the maximum-weight edge of that cycle is not included in the minimum
spanning tree of G.
